pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. In the south
   B. In the north
   C. In the east
   D. In the west

2. Which is the correct way to write the in-between point that is between south and west? (1 mark)
   A. South-west
   B. West-south-west
   C. West-south
   D. Sowest

3. How many cardinal points are there on a compass? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Two
   C. Six
   D. Four

4. What does a map key explain? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the map maker
   B. The date of the map
   C. The meaning of the colours and symbols
   D. The weather

5. A county is divided into smaller parts called what? (1 mark)
   A. Oceans
   B. Sub-counties
   C. Continents
   D. Countries

6. What is a plateau? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A deep valley
   C. A coast
   D. High land that is flat on top

7. Which physical feature is best for building roads, towns and farms easily? (1 mark)
   A. A waterfall
   B. A steep mountain
   C. A deep valley
   D. A plain

8. How can you keep safe from the sun in the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid drinking water
   B. Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   C. Play in the hottest part of the day
   D. Stay in the sun all day

9. During which season do fishermen often dry fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Dry season
   B. Rainy season
   C. No season
   D. Flood season

10. Which of these is a good? (1 mark)
   A. Teaching
   B. Driving a matatu
   C. Nursing
   D. A pair of shoes

11. On a dot map where one dot means 500 people, an area has 4 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 2,000
   B. 20,000
   C. 4,500
   D. 400

12. Why do herders in dry areas not live crowded in one place? (1 mark)
   A. They do not use water
   B. They move with animals to look for water and grass
   C. They have no families
   D. They dislike roads

13. Which type of area in Kenya usually has few people for its size? (1 mark)
   A. Busy lakeshores
   B. Highlands around Mount Kenya
   C. Dry areas in the far north
   D. Big cities

14. Which area is most likely to be sparsely populated? (1 mark)
   A. A lakeshore with fish
   B. A very dry area with little rain
   C. A fertile highland
   D. A busy town

15. What does population distribution mean? (1 mark)
   A. How many trees are in an area
   B. How tall the mountains are
   C. How much rain falls
   D. How people are spread out in an area

16. Where might you see a school motto? (1 mark)
   A. On a rain cloud
   B. In the sky
   C. On the badge or gate
   D. In a river

17. Which of these is a school value? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Honesty
   C. Cheating
   D. Stealing

18. What is the history of a school? (1 mark)
   A. The school timetable
   B. The story of how it started and changed
   C. The school menu
   D. The school bell

19. Which county is famous for its tea farms? (1 mark)
   A. Marsabit
   B. Lamu
   C. Turkana
   D. Kericho

20. What is the raw material for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Sugarcane
   B. Tea leaves
   C. Milk
   D. Wheat

21. What is a raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A finished product
   B. A machine
   C. A material used to make something new
   D. A worker

22. Which colour is best for a road safety bib? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. Grey
   C. Dark brown
   D. Bright orange or yellow

23. What is a citizen? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of law
   B. A type of school
   C. A visitor who never returns
   D. A member of a country or community with rights and duties

24. Which action shows cleanliness? (1 mark)
   A. Spitting in class
   B. Throwing rubbish on the ground
   C. Putting litter in the bin
   D. Writing on walls

25. What is cyberbullying? (1 mark)
   A. Reading a book
   B. Playing a computer game
   C. Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone
   D. Writing a letter

26. Which of these is a right of a school citizen? (1 mark)
   A. To break rules
   B. To steal
   C. To bully others
   D. To learn in a safe place

27. What does punctuality mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking loudly
   B. Arriving late
   C. Arriving on time
   D. Running fast

28. What does listening do for peace? (1 mark)
   A. It makes people angry
   B. It wastes time
   C. It helps people to understand each other
   D. It starts fights

29. What is an election? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of game
   B. A school holiday
   C. A process where people vote to choose leaders
   D. A prayer

30. What is a mock election? (1 mark)
   A. A game with no rules
   B. A practice election
   C. A school holiday
   D. A real national election

31. What should you do if your candidate loses? (1 mark)
   A. Spread rumours
   B. Fight
   C. Accept the results peacefully
   D. Refuse to work with the winner

32. Who leads the meetings of the assembly of pupils? (1 mark)
   A. The gatekeeper
   B. The cook
   C. The driver
   D. The Speaker

33. Which minister would deal with dirty toilets? (1 mark)
   A. Library
   B. Health and sanitation
   C. Sports
   D. Music

34. What do clan elders do? (1 mark)
   A. Cook school lunch
   B. Repair roads
   C. Keep customs and settle disputes
   D. Sell tickets

35. Who is a leader? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger
   B. A person who breaks rules
   C. A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   D. A machine

36. What is a community? (1 mark)
   A. A school subject
   B. A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   C. A type of crop
   D. A kind of animal

37. What does MCA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Mayor of Central Area
   B. Master of County Affairs
   C. Minister of County Administration
   D. Member of the County Assembly

38. How many MCAs does each ward elect? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. Ten
   C. Fifty
   D. One

39. Why do we have county governments? (1 mark)
   A. To end services
   B. To stop elections
   C. To bring services closer to the people
   D. To close schools

40. Who leads the meetings of the county assembly? (1 mark)
   A. The driver
   B. The governor
   C. The chief
   D. The Speaker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give two reasons why farmers plant crops at the start of the rainy season. (2 marks)

42. Name three kinds of community leaders. (3 marks)

43. Explain three elements of democracy and give an example of each in school. (5 marks)

44. Write a peace message and explain how it can help other pupils. (4 marks)

45. Who is the patron of a Children's Government? (2 marks)

46. What is meant by a densely populated area? (2 marks)

47. State three benefits of interdependence in a county. (3 marks)

48. Explain why it is important to keep records of income and costs. (3 marks)

49. Write a short note to invite a resource person to talk about a historic place in your county. Include the reason and the date. (5 marks)

50. Explain what interdependence means and give one example. (3 marks)

51. Give three ethical practices in managing a school enterprise. (3 marks)

52. Name four members of a typical Children's Government. (4 marks)

53. List four factors a company thinks about before building a factory. (4 marks)

54. State three things that spoil peace in school. (3 marks)

55. Give three questions to ask when choosing a school enterprise project. (3 marks)

56. Explain the difference between the size of a county and its population. (3 marks)

57. Explain why Kenya does not have summer and winter. (2 marks)

58. Give three reasons why historic built environments are important. (3 marks)

59. Explain three rules of good digital citizenship. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — In the west
   The sun sets in the west.

2. A — South-west
   We say the north or south word first, so it is south-west.

3. D — Four
   There are four cardinal points: north, east, south and west.

4. C — The meaning of the colours and symbols
   The key tells what each line, colour and symbol stands for.

5. B — Sub-counties
   Counties are divided into sub-counties, and sub-counties into wards.

6. D — High land that is flat on top
   A plateau is a raised area with a flat top.

7. D — A plain
   Flat land is easy to build on and farm.

8. B — Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   These habits protect us from heat.

9. A — Dry season
   Dry sunny days are best for drying fish.

10. D — A pair of shoes
   Goods are things we can touch and use.

11. A — 2,000
   4 x 500 = 2,000.

12. B — They move with animals to look for water and grass
   Herding needs large areas of pasture.

13. C — Dry areas in the far north
   Dry northern areas are sparsely populated.

14. B — A very dry area with little rain
   Dry areas make farming and water supply hard.

15. D — How people are spread out in an area
   Distribution is about where people live.

16. C — On the badge or gate
   Mottos are often on badges and gates.

17. B — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive value.

18. B — The story of how it started and changed
   History tells how the school began and grew.

19. D — Kericho
   Kericho is a major tea growing area.

20. A — Sugarcane
   Sugar is made from sugarcane.

21. C — A material used to make something new
   Raw materials are used to make products.

22. D — Bright orange or yellow
   Bright colours are easy to see.

23. D — A member of a country or community with rights and duties
   Citizens belong to a community and have rights and duties.

24. C — Putting litter in the bin
   Using bins keeps the school clean.

25. C — Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone
   Cyberbullying is bullying online.

26. D — To learn in a safe place
   Learning safely is a right.

27. C — Arriving on time
   Punctual people arrive on time.

28. C — It helps people to understand each other
   Listening helps solve conflicts.

29. C — A process where people vote to choose leaders
   Elections choose leaders.

30. B — A practice election
   A mock election teaches how voting works.

31. C — Accept the results peacefully
   Accepting results is part of democracy.

32. D — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads meetings.

33. B — Health and sanitation
   Health and sanitation looks after cleanliness.

34. C — Keep customs and settle disputes
   Clan elders guard customs and settle quarrels.

35. C — A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   Leaders guide and help.

36. B — A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   People in a community share a market, a school or customs.

37. D — Member of the County Assembly
   MCA is a Member of the County Assembly.

38. D — One
   Each ward elects one MCA.

39. C — To bring services closer to the people
   Counties bring services near to people.

40. D — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads the assembly.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rain gives the seeds water to grow, and the wet soil is soft to dig.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Religious leaders, clan elders and village elders. Accept chiefs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each kind.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Equality: one vote each. Freedom of expression: giving opinions in class. Majority rule: choosing a game by most votes. Award marks for each element and example.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct element with example, up to 5.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Talk, do not fight. It reminds pupils to solve problems with words, so there are fewer fights and everyone feels safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear message, 1 mark for correct language, 2 marks for the explanation.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The patron is a teacher who guides and advises the pupil leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a teacher, 1 mark for guides the pupil leaders.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: An area where many people live close together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many people, 1 mark for close together.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: People get goods and services they cannot make, people help each other in trouble, and the county develops faster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: To know whether there is profit or loss, to show honesty, and to plan better next time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: A polite greeting, the name of the person, the reason for the invitation, the date and time, and a thank-you at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Interdependence means people depend on and help each other. For example, a farmer grows food and a trader sells it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example, 1 mark for showing both sides need each other.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Be honest with money and customers, be fair in sharing work and rewards, and care for the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each practice.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: President, deputy president, Speaker, and class representatives. Accept cabinet members or secretary.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each member.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Raw materials, market, transport, and water and power. Accept workers or land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bullying, fighting and spreading rumours. Accept stealing or discrimination.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do people want it? Do we have the materials and skills? Is it safe? Can we earn more than we spend?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Size is the area of land a county covers. Population is the number of people who live there. A big county can have few people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size, 1 mark for population, 1 mark for the difference or example.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kenya lies on the equator, so the temperature changes little through the year. Our seasons depend mainly on rain and on how high the land is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the equator idea, 1 mark for rain or height.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: They teach us history, they give us identity and pride, and they bring tourists and income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult before going online, do not share private information, and be kind and never bully online.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.
